title: How Trak works
intro: Trak is where you plan your season, run each week, and let players and parents see how they are getting on. This page shows where everything is.
week1: Home shows what needs you: a match to evaluate, a register to take, a player who needs attention.
week2: Schedule holds your trainings, matches and other events. Add one with +.
week3: An event stays a draft until you publish it. Once it is published, players and parents see the time, the place, the kit and your note.
week4: Families can tell you a player can't make it. You see it on the event.
squad1: Squad lists your players. Open a player to set their positions, roles and objectives.
squad2: Formations keeps the shapes you play, ready to use for a match.
matches1: Before a match: the logistics, then the game plan: the line-up, each player's job and your tactics.
matches2: After a match: the evaluation. Add the result and a word on each player, then publish it.
matches3: Players and parents see the game plan and the evaluation only once you share or publish them.
training1: Plan a session from drills, fitted to the number of players you have.
training2: Who's here is the register. Notes keep what happened.
training3: Drills is the library: search it, keep drills in My drills, or browse the three kinds of practice.
season1: Set the season up once: the squad's objectives, each player's positions and objectives, and how often you evaluate.
season2: An objective is Met or Not yet. Each player and their parents see the player's own.
assess1: Assess player, from +, records how a player is doing and a message for them.
assess2: Save it as a draft, or publish it for the player and their parents to read.
families1: Players and parents see only what you publish or share. Drafts and your private notes stay with you.
settings1: Language: English or Ελληνικά, just for you.
settings2: Notifications: choose which alerts Trak sends you.
